policy.rule: Keep only reusable identity/mechanical concepts independent of class/archetype names. Class, faction, and archetype labels belong in route/narrative metadata.
policy.normalizationWarning: NORMALIZE identifies the intended canonical concept but does not authorize blind migration of every historical assignment; assignments must be re-derived from canonical rule meaning.
policy.replacementWarning: DELETE replacement arrays are decomposition guidance, not automatic per-record mappings.

decisions.rationale: Legacy scoring role is too broad and over-applied to 491 Talents. Re-derive actual offensive mechanics from rules instead of preserving a role label.
Reusable mechanical concept: movement, placement, adjacency, range-band, or battlefield-location manipulation. Independent of class/archetype identity.
Role noun duplicates the existing reusable semantic/mechanical concept `control`. Historical assignments must still be revalidated; do not bulk-map blindly.
Role noun duplicates the broader reusable `defense` concept. Historical assignments require revalidation.
Useful broad mechanical-domain tag for options whose identity is skill use, skill checks, skill access, or broad skill enhancement.
Class/order identity belongs in route/narrative data. Mechanical meaning should be expressed by actual Force/lightsaber/etc. concepts.
Class label, not a mechanic. Re-express through actual fieldcraft/exploration mechanics.
Class label is too broad. Mechanical identity varies and should be derived from the rule.
Class label is not reusable mechanics; actual combat expression should carry the signal.
Role noun maps cleanly to existing Phase 11 semantic concept `leadership`; individual Talent assignments still require evidence.
Class label, not mechanics. Preserve actual social/leadership mechanics instead.
Narrative/archetype identity rather than a discrete mechanic. Specific Force domains are more descriptive.
Broad role label. The useful mechanical identity is pursuit/tracking/target acquisition.
Prestige/class-archetype label. Decompose into actual hunting/combat mechanics.
Archetype/role label. Mechanical style is better represented by its component mechanics.
Role label is ambiguous. Actual trigger/reactive mechanics should be tagged directly.
Faction/organization identity belongs in narrative/affiliation taxonomy, not shared mechanical ontology.
Compound archetype label. The reusable mechanics are anti-Force interaction and pursuit/targeting.
Archetype/tree label, not a reusable mechanic. Preserve actual play pattern instead.
Class/archetype identity belongs in route data; mechanics are represented by Force-domain concepts.
Archetype/organization identity; decompose to actual Force/hunting/social mechanics.
Narrative experience label with no stable mechanical meaning; use the actual mechanics.
